# Automate the balance-tuning loop: baseline, single-edit, re-run and diff

> **Headline:** Add a `--tune` mode to the batch-evaluation CLI that runs a
> baseline batch, applies one declarative CSV edit, re-runs the *identical*
> sweep and writes a versioned before/after comparison with per-metric deltas
> and a readable summary — so a tuning attempt becomes one auditable,
> repeatable command instead of a manual chore.

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** feature · **Discovered from:** <<AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW>>

## Problem statement

The automated-balancing framework (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) provides the *evidence*
(batch reports with distribution statistics) but the *loop* around it is still
manual and error-prone. A designer who wants to tune a knob must, by hand:
(1) run a baseline batch, (2) edit a CSV, (3) re-run the identical command,
(4) diff the JSON/text reports and interpret per-metric deltas across a table
of distributions. Human error creeps in exactly where the tool exists to remove
it: forgetting to keep seeds identical, comparing reports from different batch
configs, or misreading which metrics actually moved. The acceptance-verification
run already had to do this diff by hand (see docs/BALANCING.md §Acceptance-verification run).

There is no automation that: records a baseline, applies a single proposed edit
(guided), re-runs against the *same* seeds/config, and produces a per-metric
before/after comparison with guidance on whether each delta looks like the
intended effect.

## Users

- **As a game designer / maintainer**, I want to run one command that (baseline → edit → re-run → compare) reports exactly which balance metrics moved and by how much, so tuning becomes a fast, auditable loop instead of a manual chore.
- **As a producer**, I want a durable, repeatable record of each tuning attempt (edit, config snapshot, before/after reports) so balance history can be reviewed and reverted.

## Expected behaviour

- A `--tune` mode on the existing `scripts/evaluate.mjs` entry point (Q1-b)
  that:
  1. Runs the baseline batch (identical seeds/config/policy) and captures the report.
  2. Applies a single, **declarative** CSV edit supplied by the caller
     (e.g. `--set enemy-configs.csv boss.health=6`) — Q2-a; the tool can
     **restore** the original file on completion so the checkout stays clean.
  3. Re-runs the identical batch and emits a **before/after comparison**
     artifact (per-metric deltas: mean/median/stdDev per distribution, plus
     per-archetype kill and per-upgrade deltas) alongside both full reports.
  4. Prints a human-readable summary identifying the metrics that moved beyond
     a **relative ±10% default threshold** on mean/median (configurable via
     `--threshold`) — Q3-a — and flags distribution-shape changes (e.g. stdDev
     growth = variance increase, median shifts).
- No production runtime impact; all new logic stays in the dev/eval layer
  (`src/ai/eval/`, Node shell). Determinism guarantees are preserved
  byte-for-byte.

## Suggested approach

- Reuse the existing irreproducibility guard: the comparison must verify both batches used identical sweep configuration (seeds, policies, ticks, dt, sampleEveryTicks) before reporting deltas — an empty diff check confirms no side effects.
- Pure diff/aggregation logic in the TS core (`src/ai/eval/`) with a thin shell wrapper in `scripts/evaluate.mjs`; no wall-clock or I/O in the pure core (same constraint as the epic).
- Where CSV edit support lands, reuse the shared loaders (`src/core/configStore.ts` via `hydrateBalanceConfig` from `src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ts`) so the re-run reads the edited values.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1: One-command loop.** A documented `--tune` command runs baseline, applies one declarative CSV edit, re-runs with an identical sweep, and writes three artifacts: baseline report, candidate report, and a versioned before/after comparison (per-metric count/mean/median/min/max/stdDev deltas, per-archetype and per-upgrade deltas).
- **AC2: Same-sweep guard.** The tool refuses to compare batches whose sweep configuration (seeds, policies, ticks, dt, sampleEveryTicks) differs, and errors on a non-empty byte-diff of identical-config re-runs (detects side effects).
- **AC3: Deterministic comparison.** Same edit + same seeds yields a byte-identical comparison artifact; independently-derived (empty) deltas are zero.
- **AC4: Safe restore.** After the run the CSV is byte-identical to its pre-run state on success **and** failure paths (or the user opted into keeping the edit), verified by test; the working tree is clean unless the user says otherwise.
- **AC5: Readable summary.** The text output flags metrics that moved beyond a configurable threshold (relative ±10% mean/median default) and notes distribution-shape changes (stdDev/median shifts), with the same statistics echoed in the machine-readable artifact.
- **AC6: Tests.** Pure comparison/aggregation, the same-sweep guard, safe restore and determinism are covered by unit tests; no wall-clock/IO leaks into the pure core.
- **AC7: Documentation.** `docs/BALANCING.md` gains a `Tuning loop (baseline → edit → re-run → compare)` section with the worked example; README references it.
- **AC8: Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.
- **AC9: All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (e.g. `docs/EVALUATION.md` if the CLI flags there are extended).

## Constraints

- **Determinism (preserve AH-0MUY08XLD009K4W4 AC5).** Every run derives from a seed; no wall clock; the before/after comparison is reproducible byte-for-byte for the same edit + seeds.
- **Dev/eval only.** No production runtime impact; `src/ai/eval/` stays pure (no I/O, no wall clock); filesystem work (CSV edit/restore, artifact writes) stays in the Node shell (`scripts/evaluate.mjs`).
- **Single source of truth.** The re-run reads the edited values through the shared config loaders (`src/core/configStore.ts` / `hydrateBalanceConfig`), never a divergent copy.
- **Gym↔game parity.** Any shared gameplay behaviour exercised by the tune loop must come from the shared core; the tune loop is a dev tool like the gyms.
- **No PII.** Reuse the existing telemetry schema and redaction policy.
- **Bounded resources.** Two batches (baseline + candidate) must not exhaust memory; reuse the batch runner's incremental aggregation.
- **Checkout hygiene.** The CSV restore must leave the working tree clean on success **and** failure unless the user opts in to keeping the edit (AC4).

## Existing state

- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — thin Node shell (Vite SSR module loader, file I/O); already parses `--batch`, `--games`, `--policies`, `--seed(s)`, `--ticks`, `--dt`, `--sample-every`, `--out`, `--json`; writes `balance-report.json`, `balance-report.txt`, `runs.jsonl` under `--out` (default `eval-output/`, git-ignored).
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` — `runBatch` sweeps seeds × policies deterministically; the batch config (seeds, policies, ticks, dt, sampleEveryTicks) is recorded in `BatchOutput.json`.
- `src/ai/eval/balanceStats.ts`-family extraction (`metrics.ts`) and aggregation; `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`-versioned `BalanceRunStats` / `BalanceAggregate` (`src/ai/eval/types.ts`) with `DistributionStats` (count/mean/median/min/max/stdDev), per-archetype `enemiesKilledByArchetype` and per-upgrade `upgradesSelected`.
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — stable serialisation + human-readable summary.
- `src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ts` / `src/core/configStore.ts` — `hydrateBalanceConfig()` loads the real `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`, `ship-config.csv`, `difficulty-curves.csv`; `ENEMY_CSV_PATH` etc. exported.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — documents the batch runner; its §Acceptance-verification run shows the (manual) CSV-edit diff that this item automates.
- The batch report already hashes the config and records seeds, so the same-sweep guard's inputs exist today.

## Desired change

1. Extend `scripts/evaluate.mjs` with a `--tune` mode (Q1-b) that chains baseline → single declarative edit → re-run → compare in one command.
2. Add declarative CSV-edit support (`--set <file>.<field>=<value>`, Q2-a) with guaranteed restore (AC4).
3. Add pure diff/aggregation logic in `src/ai/eval/` producing a versioned before/after comparison artifact (per-metric deltas, per-archetype/per-upgrade deltas).
4. Emit a human-readable summary flagging metrics moved beyond the configurable ±10% relative threshold and noting shape changes (stdDev/median) (AC5).
5. Enforce the same-sweep guard (AC2) and determinism (AC3).
6. Document the tuning loop in `docs/BALANCING.md` with the worked example; reference from README (AC7).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — new `--tune` mode: orchestrate baseline/edit/re-run/compare, CSV edit + restore, artifact writes (shell layer only).
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` or new `src/ai/eval/tune.ts` — pure tuning-loop core: same-sweep guard, before/after comparison + aggregation, determinism.
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — versioned before/after comparison types (deltas per metric/archetype/upgrade).
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — comparison rendering (readable summary + stable JSON).
- `src/util/csvEdit.ts` (new, shell-adjacent) — declarative single-field CSV edit with restore; or handled inside the `.mjs` shell.
- `src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ts` / `src/core/configStore.ts` — reused via `hydrateBalanceConfig` so the re-run reads edited values.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — new `Tuning loop (baseline → edit → re-run → compare)` section; README reference.
- Tests: new unit tests alongside `src/ai/eval/engine.test.ts` / `report.test.ts`; CLI shell tests next to `scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts`.

## Related work

- **Epic: Automated Balancing** (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) — completed; this item closes the loop around it.
- **Extend the headless arena to the full campaign** (AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A) — open; once landed, per-wave/per-upgrade fields in the schema become populated and the tune loop's per-upgrade deltas become fully meaningful; not blocking this item (the loop diffs whatever the arena reports).
- **Periodically validate the human experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) — in progress; the tune loop and the validation share the same versioned balance-statistics schema and will interoperate (tune → re-baseline → validate).
- **Collect balance statistics from human player games** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — completed; shared schema consumer.

(Also see the automated related-work report appended to the item description.)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: CSV edit corrupts the checkout.** Mitigated by AC4 (restore on success and failure paths, tested; explicit opt-out to keep the edit).
- **Risk: comparing incompatible batches produces misleading deltas.** Mitigated by AC2 same-sweep guard (refuse on differing seeds/policies/ticks/dt/sampleEveryTicks) plus the empty byte-diff side-effect check.
- **Risk: "the intended effect" is subjective.** The tool reports and flags, it does not assert intent; the threshold default (±10% relative on mean/median) is configurable and documented.
- **Risk: scope creep** (interactive edit prompt, multi-edit batches, auto-apply best candidate, wave/upgrade tuning once the campaign arena lands). Recorded as follow-up opportunities, not in scope here.
- **Assumption: the current arena output is sufficient** for a useful first tuning loop (wave/upgrade fields may still be unpopulated until AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A; per-archetype and minerals/survival deltas are already meaningful).
- **Assumption: `--tune` reuses the existing batch flags** (`--games`, `--policies`, `--seeds`, `--ticks`, `--dt`, `--sample-every`, `--out`) with no new sweep semantics.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Entry point — extend `scripts/evaluate.mjs` with a `--tune` mode, or add a new peer `scripts/balance-tune.mjs`? **Recommended:** peer script (clearer separation)." — Answer (operator): "b" — extend `scripts/evaluate.mjs` with a `--tune` mode. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- Q2: "Edit interface for v1 — declarative `--set` only, or also an interactive prompt? **Recommended:** declarative `--set` only (deterministic, scriptable, testable without a TTY)." — Answer (operator): "a" — declarative `--set` only for v1; interactive prompt deferred. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- Q3: "'Moved significantly' default threshold — relative ±10% of baseline mean/median, absolute per-metric defaults, or relative + stdDev growth flag? **Recommended:** relative ±10% (scale-free across metrics)." — Answer (operator): "a" — relative ±10% default on mean/median, configurable via `--threshold`; stdDev/median shape-flagging retained per AC5. Source: interactive reply, this session.
data.title: Automate the balance-tuning loop: baseline, single-edit, re-run and diff

# Wormhole stays visible on some waves

## Problem statement

On some (apparently unpatterned) waves the wormhole spawn VFX remains on
screen after every enemy has fully arrived — its close animation never runs
and the graphic stays visible into the next wave. There is no reliable manual
reproduction yet; a root-cause analysis (RCA) is required to identify and fix
the lifecycle bug.

## Users

- **Primary: players** of the shipped game (`PlayScene`). "As a player I expect
  the wormhole that announces each enemy wave to disappear once all enemies
  have arrived, so stale VFX never clutters the arena."
- **Secondary: gym users/developers.** Gym scenes must match the game's spawn
  VFX lifecycle per the gym↔game parity convention (AGENTS.md).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **RCA documented** — the actual root cause is identified (via a
   deterministic regression test that reproduces the stuck wormhole and fails
   before the fix, passes after), and recorded in the work item.
2. **Wormhole always closes** — whenever a wave's enemies have all finished
   growing, the wormhole's close animation runs to completion and the
   container is destroyed and removed from the effects registry — in
   `PlayScene` and every gym formation scene.
3. **At most one live wormhole** — opening a new wormhole (any `spawnWave` /
   formation respawn / transition end) first closes any still-open previous
   wormhole; no path may overwrite `_spawnWormhole` while another is live.
4. **Close survives transitions & respawns** — a wave/level/boss transition,
   wave timeout, wipe→respawn or run reset that begins while the wormhole is
   open still results in a closed, destroyed wormhole (close must not depend
   only on the non-transition update tick).
5. **Gym↔game parity** — the gym formation scenes (including wipe→respawn and
   carry-over paths) enforce the same wormhole lifecycle as the game; a
   regression test covers at least one gym scene alongside `PlayScene`.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes —
   `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §2.7 (wormhole spawn animation)
   and relevant code comments.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The wormhole timing contract is unchanged: 1 s open + 1.5 s grow + 0.5 s
  close = 3 s spawn-protection window (existing constants in
  `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`).
- No change to spawn positions, wave pacing or gameplay behaviour — this is a
  VFX lifecycle fix only.
- Shared logic must live in the shared core / shared VFX module, consumed by
  both the game and the gyms (parity rule; repo duplicate-body guard).
- Keep the existing deterministic test seams (`finishSpawnAnimations()`,
  `scene.tick(dt)`) working — they are relied on across the scene test
  suites.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene.spawnWave()` opens one wormhole at the first spawn position and
  registers it in `wormholeEffects`; `_updateSpawnAnimations()` closes it once
  `!anySpawning` — but that method is only invoked on non-transition frames
  (`update()` gates it behind `!transitioning`).
- `_onTransitionComplete()` calls `spawnWave()` unconditionally; `spawnWave()`
  has **no guard** to close a previously-open `_spawnWormhole` before
  overwriting it.
- `resetRunState()` sets `_spawnWormhole = null` without destroying the
  container.
- Gyms: `respawnFormation()` / `respawnWithCarriedSurvivors()` rebuild the
  formation without closing an open wormhole (and without re-opening one for
  the fresh entities).

## Desired change

- Close any live wormhole as part of a single, shared lifecycle invariant:
  exactly one live wormhole; it closes (scale→0, alpha→0, destroy, remove
  from registry) once its wave's entities have finished growing — regardless
  of transitions, timeouts, respawns or resets — and any new wormhole first
  cleans up the previous one.
- Add deterministic regression tests covering at least: (a) transition /
  timeout beginning mid-spawn, (b) second `spawnWave()` while one wormhole is
  still live, (c) a gym respawn path.
- Fix in the shared VFX/helper layer where the game and gyms already share
  code; update docs §2.7.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_updateSpawnAnimations()` (close gating),
  `spawnWave()` (open without closing previous), `resetRunState()`/`_loseLife`
  paths.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `respawnFormation()`,
  `respawnWithCarriedSurvivors()`, `_updateSpawnAnimations()`.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — shared open/close lifecycle (candidate home
  for a shared "close if open" guard).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `wormholeEffects` registry init/teardown.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (describe "wormhole spawn animation") and
  `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` (parity describe) — regression
  tests.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §2.7 documentation update.

## Related work

- AH-0MURBER4L00821RR (completed) — the wormhole spawn-animation feature that
  introduced this code; the lifecycle bug is a regression/gap of that feature.
- AH-0MV8BR9Y70079TKC (open) — "Wormhole appears away from player";
  different symptom, same VFX; not blocking, do not absorb.
- AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW (open) — "Enemies should emerge from the wormhole";
  related aesthetics, not blocking, do not absorb.
- AH-0MV9G113S009B37I (in-progress) — "Mystery UFO has no visible
  representation"; picked up by the find-related keyword search but not
  directly related — noted for traceability only.
- AGENTS.md "Gym↔game parity" convention — the parity requirement for this
  fix.
- Automated find-related report (see related-work comment on the work item).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **RCA is the gating risk** — a deterministic repro must be built first;
  without it the fix may address a symptom rather than the leak. Mitigation:
  reproduce the transition/overwrite and respawn paths in tests.
- **Assumption:** the intended lifecycle is exactly one live wormhole per
  wave; over-closing is harmless (close is idempotent after destroy).
- **Risk:** gating the close on the non-transition tick is the core defect —
  the fix must not depend on any single update path.
- **Scope creep:** wormhole positioning (AH-0MV8BR9Y70079TKC) and
  emerge-from-centre (AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW) are tracked separately — out of
  scope here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No interview questions were asked: the seed context ("wormhole stays visible,
  RCA and resolve") combined with code inspection of `PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene`, `wormholeSpawn.ts` and the worklog sufficed to draft
  this brief. Any reproduction specifics still unknown (the item notes "I
  cannot discern a pattern") are addressed by the RCA-driven regression test
  (AC1) rather than by further questions.
- OPEN QUESTION: whether the operator can supply a recording/level where the
  stuck wormhole was observed would narrow the RCA; not required to proceed.

# Test matrix and shared fixtures for the collector-drone path

## Summary

Define the verification foundation for the visible collector drone: a test
matrix mapping every parent acceptance criterion to the test that verifies
it, plus shared fixtures (mineral-field builder, mock/stepped clock, drone
spawn seam helpers) that the feature tests consume. Landed **green** first as
the leading `task`, matching the established pattern for shared-core
behaviour work (cf. AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB).

## Target outcome

Every parent AC of AH-0MV9G113S009B37I has a named, runnable verification;
feature tasks reuse the fixtures instead of inventing ad-hoc scaffolding.

## Minimal implementation

- Add a test matrix (in a comment or dedicated test section) mapping each
  parent AC to its test: spawn-one-no-payout (AC1), seek/collect/return/payout
  and lifetime/capacity (AC2), monotonic level resolution (AC3), permanent
  timer vs single field spawn (AC4), destruction variants (AC5), gym parity +
  equivalence + docs assertion (AC6), docs coverage (AC7).
- Add shared fixtures used by the drone tests: a seeded mineral-field builder
  (clear of the ship start), a stepped/mock clock for timer tests, and small
  helpers to manufacture a `mystery_ufo` drop.
- Update existing tests that pin the retired instant bounty (e.g.
  `effects.test.ts` `mystery_ufo` burst cases, `powerUpLevels.test.ts` score
  axis) so the suite stays green as the instant path is removed.
- Fixture/test scaffolding compiles and the suite stays green (no red commit:
  the drone behaviour tests land within their implementing features, TDD).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test matrix exists mapping every parent AC of AH-0MV9G113S009B37I to its
  verifying test; the matrix is referenced from the fixture file header.
- Shared fixtures (mineral field, mock clock, drop manufacture) exist and are
  used by at least one test in a later feature.
- Existing instant-bounty tests are updated so the suite is green after this
  item lands (no red commit).
- The changed fixtures/tests follow the repo's test-writing guidelines.

# Planning Complete — AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715

Decomposed into 6 child work items (test-first, dependency-ordered), each a
deliverable vertical slice reusing the existing batch runner (`runBatch`),
shared `BalanceAggregate` schema and `stableStringify`:

| Child | Title | Type | Effort | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AH-0MVBNIS59000MXW1 | Tune-comparison core: versioned before/after deltas | feature | Extra Small | Medium |
| AH-0MVBNISIZ003C20U | Same-sweep guard: refuse cross-config comparisons | feature | Extra Small | Low |
| AH-0MVBNISWE009QFBL | Declarative CSV edit with guaranteed restore | feature | Extra Small | Medium |
| AH-0MVBNITA0005VQGN | `--tune` CLI: baseline, edit, re-run and compare | feature | Extra Small | Medium |
| AH-0MVBNLLPI004QI2F | Tuning-loop docs: BALANCING.md, README, EVALUATION.md | docs | Extra Small | Low |
| AH-0MVBNLM2V008XC8T | End-to-end tune-loop verification + full suite | task | Extra Small | Medium |

**Dependency edges:** c2→c1; c4→c1,c2,c3; c5→c4; c6→c4,c5. All 9 parent
acceptance criteria are covered by children (tree-coverage review: 100%,
`proceed`, no auto-closed gaps).

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-16 ~23:57Z — pre-check `plan-if-needed` → `plan` (Small/Medium above
  skip threshold, which requires risk Low). Plan-approval gate → `false`
  (requires Extra Large + High/Severe); no approval pause.
- 2026-10-17 — six automated review stages run on the draft (AC alignment,
  completeness incl. Key Files validation, sequencing/deps, scope sizing,
  acceptance/testability, polish/handoff); one unambiguous fix applied
  (verification item Key Files path).
- 2026-10-17 — 6 children created, dependency edges wired, effort/risk
  estimated per child via the effort-and-risk skill, coverage review advanced
  stage to `plan_complete` (status `open`).

## Appendix: addendum (planning session)

No new clarifying questions were required: the description's Appendix Q1–Q3
(extend `scripts/evaluate.mjs` with `--tune`; declarative `--set` only;
relative ±10% mean/median default, `--threshold`) were reused as-is for this
planning session. Design decisions recorded for implementation:

- Comparison artifact is versioned via a schema-version constant + the
  existing stable key-sorted serialisation (no wall clock), not a timestamp.
- `--keep-edit` is the explicit opt-out that disables restore (heads AC4).
- The same-sweep guard compares `BalanceReport.config` (seeds, policies,
  ticks, dt, sampleEveryTicks) and detects side effects via per-run
  `recordsHash` — inputs that exist in the report today.
- CSV edit/restore helper is pure string-level (`src/util/csvEdit.ts`);
  filesystem work stays in the Node shell, matching the epic's purity rule.
- Re-run reads edited values through the shared loaders
  (`hydrateBalanceConfig`/`loadBalanceConfig`) — no divergent copy.
